The Indian Constitution borrowed the Cabinet System from the British Constitutional System.
The Indian Constitution borrowed Prerogative Writs from the British Constitutional System.

Article 14 provides equality before law.
Article 14 provides equal protection of the laws.
Article 14 applies to citizens.
Article 14 applies to foreigners.

The Basic Structure status of the Rule of Law was affirmed in Indira Nehru Gandhi in 1975.

The assertion that the State has inherent unlimited police powers is false.

Rule of Law represents government under law.
Rule by Law uses law as an instrument or weapon of state control.

Rule by Law represents government above law.
Equality before law is of British origin.
Equality before law is a negative concept.
Equality before law means the absence of special privilege for any individual.
Equal protection of the laws is of American origin.

Equal protection of the laws means equal treatment under equal circumstances.
Equal protection of the laws permits reasonable classification.
The phrase “Procedure Established by Law” appears in the text of Article 21.

After Maneka Gandhi in 1978, due process of law requires a law to be just, fair, and reasonable.
After Maneka Gandhi, due process of law requires freedom from procedural arbitrariness.
Constitutional Government is synonymous with Limited Government.
Constitutional Government defines power.
Constitutional Government restrains power.

Constitutional provisions prevent executive tyranny under Constitutional Government.
Public Interest Litigation promotes access to justice for disadvantaged persons.
Public Interest Litigation strengthens access to justice for disadvantaged persons.
Public Interest Litigation is not an indispensable prerequisite for the existence of the Rule of Law.
The Rule of Law existed before the evolution of Public Interest Litigation.
The Rule of Law existed through Articles 14, 32, and 226 before the evolution of Public Interest Litigation.

69.text: The Supreme Court of India is governed under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution.

Incapacity is a ground for removing a Supreme Court judge.

The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.

A curative petition prevents abuse of process.
A curative petition cures gross miscarriages of justice.
A curative petition is available after a review petition under Article 137 has been dismissed.
A Constitution Bench requires a minimum of five judges under Article 145(3).
A minimum of five judges must hear a case involving a substantial question of law concerning the interpretation of the Constitution.
A minimum of five judges must hear references under Article 143.
The Supreme Court is a Court of Record under Article 129.
The High Court is a Court of Record under Article 215.
Supreme Court decisions have evidentiary value.
Supreme Court decisions cannot be questioned in subordinate courts.
The Supreme Court has inherent power to punish for contempt of itself.
The High Court has parallel Court of Record status at the State level.
The Supreme Court Collegium consists of the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most Supreme Court judges.
The Supreme Court Collegium has a total of five members.
The Supreme Court Collegium was judicially evolved through the Three Judges Cases.
The First Judges Case occurred in 1981.
The Second Judges Case occurred in 1993.
The Third Judges Case occurred in 1998.
The Supreme Court Collegium was not created by an Act of Parliament.
The Supreme Court Collegium is not explicitly written in the Constitution.
Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes under Article 262.
Article 131 does not cover Finance Commission matters under Article 280.
Article 131 does not cover recovery of damages by a private party against the Union.
Special Leave Petitions do not lie against judgments or sentences passed by courts-martial or military tribunals under Article 136(2).
Opinions rendered by the Supreme Court to the President under Article 143 are strictly advisory.

45.text: The term “Council” in Indian Polity spans three distinct constitutional institutions.

The Vice-President is not a constituent member of Parliament.

The Union Council of Ministers aids and advises the President.

The State Council of Ministers aids and advises the Governor.

The Governor is bound by ministerial advice except in discretionary areas.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House.

The Legislative Assembly is the Lower House.
The Legislative Assembly is the Popular House.
The Legislative Council is the Upper House.

The Legislative Assembly is dissolvable.
The Legislative Assembly has a five-year term.
The State Legislative Council is a permanent body.
A member of the State Legislative Council has a six-year term.

The minimum age for membership of the Legislative Council is 30 years.
The Legislative Assembly is the sole House of introduction for a Money Bill.

The Chairman presides over the Legislative Council.
Ministers are collectively responsible only to the Lower House.
The Union Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
The Union Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to Parliament as a whole.
The Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the President or Governor.

61.text: The Consolidated Fund and financial funds are governed under Part XII of the Constitution.
Part XII covers Articles 265 to 267.
The Consolidated Fund and financial funds are governed under Part V of the Constitution.

Article 265 provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

63.text: Citizenship is governed under Part II of the Constitution.
Part II contains Articles 5 to 11 on citizenship.
Part II primarily identifies citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
The Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.
Parliament has exclusive constitutional power to regulate citizenship by law under Article 11.
Parliament has exclusive constitutional power to regulate the acquisition of citizenship.
Parliament has exclusive constitutional power to regulate the termination of citizenship.
The Citizenship Act was enacted in 1955.
The Citizenship Rules are made under Section 18 of the Citizenship Act.
State Legislatures have no power to make citizenship laws.
The President has no power to make citizenship laws.
The Election Commission has no power to make citizenship laws.
India provides for single citizenship.
India provides for a single domicile across its entire territory.
Single citizenship and single domicile are unitary features of India’s federal structure.
The USA has dual federal and state citizenship.
Article 5 deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
Article 5 requires domicile in India for citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
Article 5 recognizes birth in India as a basis for citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

Article 6 deals with the rights of persons who migrated from Pakistan to India.
Article 6 distinguishes migration before and after the permit cut-off date.

Article 7 deals with the rights of certain migrants to Pakistan.
Article 7 covers persons who migrated to Pakistan after 1 March 1947.

Article 8 deals with the rights of Persons of Indian Origin residing abroad.

Article 11 gives Parliament comprehensive power to legislate on the termination of citizenship.

Birth is a mode of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Birth-based citizenship depends on the place of birth.
Birth-based citizenship follows jus soli with modified criteria.
Descent is a mode of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Descent covers persons born outside India to Indian citizen parents.
Descent-based citizenship follows jus sanguinis.
Registration is a mode of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Registration is governed by Section 5 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
A Person of Indian Origin may acquire citizenship by registration if ordinarily resident in India for seven years before applying.
Persons married to Indian citizens may acquire citizenship by registration.
Naturalization is a mode of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Naturalization is governed by Section 6 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

Foreigners meeting character criteria may be granted citizenship by naturalization.
Incorporation of territory is a mode of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

Pondicherry is an example of territory acquired by India through incorporation of territory.
Sikkim is an example of territory acquired by India through incorporation of territory.

In the USA, only a natural-born citizen can become President.

In India, a naturalized citizen is eligible to become President of India.
Article 58 concerns eligibility to become President of India.
Depositing money in Indian banks does not confer Indian citizenship.
Purchasing property in India does not confer Indian citizenship.
Marrying a foreign citizen does not by itself revoke Indian citizenship.

Persons who were citizens of Pakistan are strictly ineligible for OCI registration.

The Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 was passed by the Lok Sabha on 9 December 2019.

The National Development Council is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body.

NITI Aayog was established in 2015.

62.text: Indian State legislatures are governed under Part VI of the Constitution.

Bihar is a bicameral State.
Maharashtra is a bicameral State.
Karnataka is a bicameral State.

The State Legislative Council cannot be dissolved.
The Council of States is a permanent body.

The Council of States cannot be abolished.
The State Legislative Assembly can be dissolved.
The State Legislative Assembly cannot be abolished.

Members of the Council of States have a 6-year term.
One-third of the members of the Council of States retire every 2 years.

The Vice-President is not a member of the Council of States.

The State Legislative Assembly initiates the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council by passing a resolution.

Parliament enacts the law for creating or abolishing a Legislative Council.

The parliamentary law for creating or abolishing a Legislative Council is passed like an ordinary bill.

A Money Bill can originate only in the Legislative Assembly.

80.text: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is governed under Part V, Chapter V of the Constitution.

The Election Commission of India is one of the four bulwarks of the democratic system.

The Comptroller and Auditor General audits all expenditure from the Consolidated Funds of States.

The Comptroller and Auditor General does not exercise day-to-day control over the exchequer.

The audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General is post-expenditure or ex-post facto.

38.text: The President summons each House of Parliament under Article 85.

Prorogation terminates a session of the House.

An Adjournment Motion suspends business for an urgent matter of public importance.
An Adjournment Motion carries an element of censure or condemnation.
An Adjournment Motion interrupts normal business.
A Starred Question requires an oral answer.

Charged Expenditure is non-votable expenditure.

Habeas Corpus means “To have the body.”

Quo-Warranto means “By what warrant/authority.”

Pardon completely absorbs the sentence.
Pardon completely removes the sentence.
Pardon completely absorbs the conviction.
Pardon completely removes the conviction.

PR-STV is used for electing the Vice-President.
